message.content:
Search this repository for every place where memo visibility is enforced — i.e., where code checks whether a user is allowed to view/access a memo based on its visibility setting (PUBLIC, PROTECTED, PRIVATE). This is NOT about setting visibility, but about enforcing access control based on visibility.

Look for patterns like:
- Checking `memo.Visibility` or `visibility` against constants like PUBLIC, PROTECTED, PRIVATE
- Filtering memos by visibility in queries
- Access denied / permission checks related to memo visibility
- Visibility checks in API handlers, RSS feeds, file servers, SSE/streaming, etc.

Search breadth: very thorough. Check all server-side code including:
- server/router/api/v1/ (gRPC handlers)
- server/router/rss/ (RSS feeds)
- server/router/fileserver/ (file serving)
- server/router/frontend/ (frontend serving)
- store/db/ (database query filtering)

Report each distinct enforcement site with the file path and line numbers.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

I now have a complete picture. Here is my report.

---

## Memo Visibility Enforcement Sites

I found **14 distinct enforcement sites** across the codebase where memo visibility controls access. These fall into three categories: (A) direct visibility checks on individual memo objects, (B) query-time filtering via `VisibilityList` or filter expressions, and (C) SSE delivery filtering.

---

### 1. `checkMemoReadAccess` -- central gatekeeper for single-memo reads

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 39-67

This is the primary reusable function. Logic:
- If visibility is not PUBLIC, requires an authenticated user.
- If visibility is PRIVATE, denies access unless the user is the creator.
- (PROTECTED implicitly allows any authenticated user through.)

**Called from:**
- `GetMemo` at line 356 (and for parent memo at line 367) in the same file.
- `ListMemoComments` at line 148 in `memo_service_comments.go`.

---

### 2. `ListMemos` query-time visibility filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`, lines 218-227

When listing memos:
- Unauthenticated user: `VisibilityList` set to `[Public]` only (line 219).
- Authenticated user viewing all creators: a filter expression `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` is appended (line 222).
- Authenticated user viewing a different user's memos: `VisibilityList` set to `[Public, Protected]` (line 225).

---

### 3. `CreateMemoComment` visibility enforcement

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`, lines 33-43

Before allowing a comment on a memo, checks if the parent memo is PRIVATE. If so, only the creator or a super-user may comment (line 41).

---

### 4. `ListMemoComments` visibility filtering of returned comments

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go`, lines 148-161

First calls `checkMemoReadAccess` on the parent memo (line 148). Then applies a visibility filter to the comment listing:
- Unauthenticated: `visibility == "PUBLIC"` (line 158).
- Authenticated: `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` (line 160).

---

### 5. `ListMemoReactions` visibility enforcement

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`, lines 29-41

Before listing reactions on a memo:
- If not PUBLIC, requires authentication (lines 30-37).
- If PRIVATE, only the creator or super-user may access (line 38).

---

### 6. `UpsertMemoReaction` visibility enforcement

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go`, lines 82-85

Before allowing a reaction on a memo:
- If PRIVATE, only the creator or super-user may react (line 83).

---

### 7. `checkAttachmentAccess` -- attachment access via memo visibility

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`, lines 419-455

For attachments linked to a memo:
- If memo is PUBLIC, access is granted (line 445).
- Otherwise requires authentication (line 449).
- If PRIVATE, only creator or super-user (line 451).

Called from `GetAttachment` at line 256.

---

### 8. `ListMemoAttachments` visibility enforcement

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go`, lines 213-224

Before listing attachments for a memo:
- If not PUBLIC, requires authentication (line 214).
- If PRIVATE, only creator or super-user (line 222).

---

### 9. `ListMemoRelations` visibility filtering

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go`, lines 107-112

When listing relations for a memo, a filter is applied to the related memos:
- Unauthenticated: `visibility == "PUBLIC"` (line 109).
- Authenticated: `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` (line 111).

---

### 10. `convertMemoFromStore` relation-loading visibility filter (converter)

**File:** `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go`, lines 182-187

When batch-loading relations for memo conversion:
- Unauthenticated: `visibility == "PUBLIC"` (line 184).
- Authenticated: `creator_id == <id> || visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` (line 186).

### 19. Database-level `VisibilityList` WHERE clause (all three drivers)

The `VisibilityList` field on `store.FindMemo` is translated to a SQL WHERE clause in each database driver. This is the mechanism through which all the query-time enforcement above actually takes effect:

- **SQLite:** `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/memo.go`, lines 96-102 -- `` `memo`.`visibility` IN (?) ``
- **PostgreSQL:** `/bench/repo/store/db/postgres/memo.go`, lines 89-95 -- `memo.visibility in ($N)`
- **MySQL:** `/bench/repo/store/db/mysql/memo.go`, lines 104-110 -- `` `memo`.`visibility` in (?) ``

The filter expressions containing `visibility in ["PUBLIC", "PROTECTED"]` are processed by the filter engine (`filter.AppendConditions`) which also generates SQL WHERE clauses in each driver (SQLite line 61, Postgres line 58, MySQL line 69).
